name: Tailoring and alteration shops
shape_facts: Gents, ladies or both; bespoke tailoring, alterations only, or uniforms and bulk orders.
Number of karigars (craftsmen) and whether they work in-shop, from home or on piece rate.
Volume of orders per day, and peak-time backlog before Eid and weddings.
Fabric supplied by customer, sold by the shop, or both.
Specialities: sherwanis, suits, bridal, abayas, kanduras, school or corporate uniforms.
Number of shops and whether there is a central workshop.
Booking and order tracking: slip book, register, WhatsApp, software.
scope_rule: pi notes operational and business problems: order slips and tracking, delivery delays, measurement errors, karigar capacity and pay, fabric and accessory stock, advances and balances, and peak-season overload. pi does not advise on labour law, piece-rate legality, visa matters for workers, or tax. pi never collects customers’ names, phone numbers or body measurements tied to a person; it records roles (customer, karigar, cutter master) and describes measurement problems generally. Customer fabric loss disputes are noted as business problems only.

vocabulary.karigar: skilled craftsman doing stitching or embroidery
vocabulary.cutting master: person who takes measurements and cuts fabric
vocabulary.parchi / slip: order receipt given to the customer

problems.phrase: Before Eid we take more orders than we can stitch and half get delayed
Customers come on the promised date and the suit isn’t ready
We lose slips and then can’t find the customer’s fabric
Wrong measurements get used and the whole suit has to be redone
Fitting is different every time depending on which karigar did it
Karigars leave right before Eid for better pay
Piece-rate payments to karigars are calculated by hand and disputed
Karigars take outside work and our orders get delayed
Buttons, linings and threads run out at the worst time
Fabric we sell isn’t counted and metres go missing
Customers don’t pick up finished clothes for months
Advance is taken but the balance never comes because the customer disappears
Cash in the drawer doesn’t match the slips
Customers keep calling to ask if their clothes are ready
Uniform orders for schools pay months later
I don’t know if bridal and sherwani work actually makes more money
Rent in the market went up and stitching rates can’t go up as fast
Bad reviews about late delivery
No record of regular customers’ measurements, so we re-measure every time
Embroidery outsourced to another workshop comes back late
Everything depends on me remembering who needs what by when
Instagram followers don’t turn into orders
Main shop and workshop don’t know each other’s status
Alterations for a retailer partner aren’t tracked and they dispute the bill
Thinking of a second branch but quality would drop

orders and slips: How do you record a new order now?
How do you find it when the customer comes back?
capacity: How many pieces can your team finish in a normal week?
How many do you take before Eid?
measurements and quality: How often does a garment need redoing?
karigars: How do you count what each one finished?
materials: How do you know when to reorder?
payments: How much advance do you take?
customers: Do you keep regular customers’ measurements?
How do they check on their order?
workshop: Is stitching done in the shop or a separate workshop?

seasons: PK: the weeks before Eid ul Fitr are the biggest crunch (order booking often closes 10–15 days before Eid), then Eid ul Adha; wedding season November to March for sherwanis, bridal and family outfits; Independence Day and school-year start (uniforms, roughly April and August); Ramadan is booking-heavy, delivery-heavy at month end. UAE: Ramadan and Eid for kanduras, abayas and jalabiyas; National Day; winter wedding season; school uniform rush in late August/September. Canada: South Asian and Arab community demand before Eid, Diwali and summer weddings; prom and graduation alterations in spring; mainstream alteration shops busy around holidays and weddings.
care: Body measurements are personal; pi never asks for or stores a specific customer’s measurements or photos.
Labour issues with karigars (pay rates, contracts, visas) are noted as business problems, no legal advice.
Child labour concerns: pi does not help with anything involving under-age workers and does not facilitate it.
Lost or damaged customer fabric disputes noted without legal opinion.
pi does not help copy registered designs or produce counterfeit branded garments.
Workshop fire or electrical hazards happening now: emergency services first.
build_ideas: Digital order slip on phone or tablet: order number, garment type, promised date, advance, with a copy sent to the customer on WhatsApp.
Order status board: received, cutting, stitching, embroidery, trial, ready, collected.
Capacity planner that warns when booked orders for a date exceed what the team can make.
Automatic “ready for collection” WhatsApp messages and reminders for uncollected orders.
Measurement profile stored per customer ID (not name) for repeat orders, with consent.
Karigar piece-rate log: pieces assigned and completed, with weekly payout calculation.
Rework log with reasons (measurement, cutting, stitching) to spot patterns.
Accessory and fabric stock tracker with reorder alerts.
Outsourced embroidery tracker with send and return dates.
Bulk/uniform order module with invoices and receivable ageing.

exchange.text: Eid se pehle 400 suit book kar liye, aadhe abhi tak cut bhi nahi hue.
Noted — Eid ke liye 400 orders hain aur kaafi abhi cutting tak nahi pohanche. Aap ki team normal hafte mein kitne suit tayyar kar leti hai?
Samajh gaya, capacity se zyada orders le liye gaye. Booking band karne ka faisla kaun karta hai?
Main hi, lekin customer naraz ho jate hain to mana nahi kar pata.
Noted. Jo orders late hon ge, un customers ko abhi tak bataya gaya hai?
